events.title: Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo Signed
events.description: The United States and Mexico signed the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo in the Mexican town of Guadalupe Hidalgo, ending the Mexican-American War. Mexico ceded about 525,000 square miles of territory, including present-day California, Nevada, Utah, and parts of Arizona, Colorado, New Mexico, and Wyoming, in exchange for $15 million.
events.significance: The treaty reshaped the map of North America, expanded the United States to the Pacific Ocean, and intensified the national debate over the extension of slavery into new territories.

events.title: First Groundhog Day Observed at Punxsutawney
events.description: The first official Groundhog Day celebration took place in Punxsutawney, Pennsylvania, where a groundhog later named Punxsutawney Phil was said to predict the remainder of winter based on whether he saw his shadow. The tradition grew from German folk customs related to Candlemas.
events.significance: Groundhog Day became one of the best-known folk traditions in North America, drawing thousands of visitors each year and inspiring the 1993 film of the same name.

events.title: German Surrender at Stalingrad
events.description: The last German forces of the Sixth Army surrendered to Soviet troops at Stalingrad, ending the Battle of Stalingrad. The battle lasted over five months and cost both sides enormous casualties, with roughly 90,000 German soldiers taken prisoner.
events.significance: Stalingrad is widely regarded as a turning point of World War II in Europe, as it marked the beginning of Germany's strategic retreat on the Eastern Front.

events.title: Serum Run to Nome
events.description: A relay of mushers and sled dog teams, including Gunnar Kaasen with his lead dog Balto, delivered diphtheria antitoxin across nearly 700 miles of harsh Alaskan terrain to Nome. The serum arrived in the early hours of February 2, after the final leg was completed.
events.significance: The run saved the isolated town of Nome from a diphtheria epidemic, drew worldwide attention to the importance of vaccination, and inspired the Iditarod sled dog race.

events.title: F. W. de Klerk Lifts Ban on the African National Congress
events.description: South African President F. W. de Klerk announced in Parliament that the ban on the African National Congress and other anti-apartheid organizations would be lifted, and that political prisoners including Nelson Mandela would be released.
events.significance: The announcement began the dismantling of apartheid, leading to Mandela's release nine days later and negotiations that culminated in multiracial democratic elections in 1994.
